name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: To reach 100% link coverage, we should integrate Kaedim's AI-powered 3D asset production into our pipeline, as it will automate the creation of high-quality assets, freeing up resources to focus on increasing link coverage. This decision prioritizes efficiency and quality over manual labor, allowing us to meet the daily 5% increase target. By adopting this approach, we're accepting the trade-off of potential initial setup costs and potential dependencies on Kaedim's technology. This trade-off is worthwhile, as it enables us to deliver concrete artifacts and complete bus tasks efficiently.

name: Scriv
text: Kaedim’s AI won’t solve the link-coverage gate—it only shifts the black box from human error to Kaedim’s model risk. The real risk is that Scope’s pre-approved thresholds now hide whether the links we’re covering are even the right ones. To settle this, we need to audit the thresholds first, then measure coverage against the bus task’s concrete artifact, not just another AI pipeline.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt Gluestack UI MCP Server to cover UI link testing. It plugs directly into our workflow with pre-approved thresholds, pushing coverage +5%/day without adding black-box risk. The trade-off is locking into Gluestack’s model, but it’s already vetted by Engineering and Data, so we avoid re-auditing thresholds.
[dispatched 2 workers: worker-2314, worker-1067 — done, dissolved]

name: Sift
text: Gluestack’s MCP Server doesn’t fix the black-box problem—it just outsources it to another model, and pre-approved thresholds still hide whether the links we’re covering are the right ones. The real risk is that we’re trading one unknown (human error) for another (model risk) without auditing the thresholds first. To settle this, we need to audit the thresholds, then measure whether the links Gluestack covers are actually the ones we need—not just the ones it can generate.

name: Scope
text: We should adopt pre-approved model thresholds set jointly by Engineering and Data, and then use Gluestack UI MCP Server to cover UI link testing. This decision allows us to leverage a vetted model while ensuring thresholds are set with joint approval, mitigating the risk of hidden errors. The trade-off is that we're accepting some level of model risk, but this is offset by the efficiency gains and quality improvements from automation. By doing so, we can push link coverage upward at the required rate while maintaining quality control.

name: Scriv
text: Scope’s pre-approved thresholds don’t audit the links—they just certify the model’s output against *its own* definition of correctness, which may not match our access gate. The real risk is that we’re optimizing for coverage metrics while still missing the links that actually block the bus task. To settle this, we need to test the thresholds against the bus task’s concrete artifact, not just the model’s confidence scores.

name: Echo
text:
DECISION: Split effort 50% Kaedim (audit transcripts + product pages against access gate) and 50% Gluestack UI MCP Server (cover UI link testing with pre-approved thresholds).

Result: Push link coverage to 100% at +5%/day while exposing hidden model risks.
Owners: Kaedim task by Reel, Gluestack task by Chisel.
